found.context:
Cancellations with 24 or more hours notice get a full deposit refund. Cancellations inside 24 hours forfeit the deposit. Rescheduling with 24+ hours notice is free. Bookings cancelled by us due to unsafe conditions are fully refunded.

Our policy is designed to be fair to both sides. With 24 or more hours notice you can reschedule for free or cancel and get the deposit back to your original payment method (Stripe takes 5-10 business days). Inside the 24-hour window the deposit is kept as a cancellation fee, since we are usually unable to refill the slot.

If we have to cancel because of dangerous conditions (very rare, but cyclonic swell or thunderstorms with lightning), you get a full refund or free rescheduling to a later date.

If you turn up on the day and conditions are smaller or messier than ideal but still safe, we run the lesson. Sri Lanka has waves every day; sometimes the smal

4. Cancellation and Refunds
4.1 Cancellation by Customer
More than 48 hours before: Full refund of the booking fee
24-48 hours before: 50% refund of the booking fee
Less than 24 hours before: No refund
No-show: No refund
4.2 Cancellation by Provider

We reserve the right to cancel or reschedule sessions due to unsafe weather or ocean conditions. In such cases, we will offer an alternative date or a full refund of the booking fee.

THE LOCAL BEHIND SANJEE SURF

Ayubowan, I'm Sanjee.

I was born in Weligama, learned to surf on a broken board my uncle fixed with resin and hope, and have spent more than two decades in this bay. Today I teach surfers from all over the world — and I still paddle out every single morning.

ISA Level 1 Instructor
Certified Lifeguard
Weligama Local

Sanjee at Weligama Bay, where it all started.

20+

3,000+

Happy students

My story

Weligama means "sandy village" in Sinhala — and that sandy bottom is exactly why this bay is one of the best places on earth to learn surfing. I caught my first wave here when I was twelve, on a board that had more dings than fiberglass. By sixteen I was showing backpackers where to paddle out. By twenty I was doing it full-time.

surf_loop_cause: assets/index-Dqm5eYLp.js: the fetch callback depends on the data state (useCallback(..., [data, toast])) and an effect runs it whenever the callback changes (useEffect(() => { fetch(); ... }, [fetch])). Each success stores a new object, so the callback changes and it fetches again, until the server answers 429. Then the catch branch shows the toast, because data is already set, and sets the error that shows 'Live data temporarily unavailable'.
